main_text.p: fimplicia medicamenta contundi, & in electuaris formam cum melle, vel sirupo conuenienter, vt rosarum acetosi atq; citri, acetosae, scabiosae, cōtinnari. Acetū ex hisquoq, concinnata p[?]stantissima sunt. Secretum magni cuiusdam Comitis, in cuius praeparatione ego addidi vincetoxicum cum momento Cemphorae. Sequentes in praeseruatione celebra[?]ssimum est, paratu a quouis facillimum vilique pretio.

Recip. baccarum iuniperi, corticibus nigris detractis, quantum lubet: folia rutae, iuglandis, desiij vel plures: Zedoariam, angelicam: quibus omnibus contufis in mortario cum melle electuarium, si [?]ē. Quia enim [?]suadet, et quoties sunt, super sub. Eodem etiam modo vsurpata theriaca cum tridati cum infignes praestant vsus, sed in curatione improbantur. Quia enim magna [?] tenuium ac calida partium, calorem febri-lem augent, quod notandum est: in primo tamen infultu ante febrim concedantur.

NB. Confueui quoq; pradistorum simplicium vaginam quandam in crassiorem pulueream redigere, fericoq; infuere s[?] interiori pilei veltiara parti, vbi cerebellum contingit & verticem anne-ctere, non tam vitiati aeris emendandi, & a cerebro repellendi, quam ejusdem corroborandi gratia.

Olea & odorife-ra vnguenta praestan-tissima. Olea quoq; & odorifera vnguenta naribus temporibusq; admota vel inuncta, ficut & cardiacam praestant vires, pulsus, manus, Spiritus ab omni contagio-ne feruant immunes.

page.notes: The scan is faint and skewed in the middle lines; the words marked [?] and the first lines of the second paragraph are uncertain readings. The Latin of the opening lines (Acetum ex hisquoq, Sequentes in praeservatione) is partly illegible, and the Recipe passage is the least certain part. The catchword "Ex Oleis" is at the foot right. The running head is "De Vita", with page number 38 at the top left. The left-margin notes are set in smaller type and their line placement is approximate.
